claims: In this pinned public software experiment, all eight complete 4 MiB CPU-upload outputs match the width-clamped table model; the raw-width model differs only for zero-width CT32 and CT16 cases. This is a synthetic software observation, not a PS2 hardware result.

The standalone public helpers disagree with the raw-width table reference in 663,552 of 1,474,560 tested width0/1 addresses; they are a separate route from actual CPU UploadImage, so their indexed mismatches must not be attributed directly to the tested CPU backend.

Among all 56 archive models, 224 extra-mip records serialize DBW0. Nine cross a vertical page boundary: four CT32, five T8, zero T4; one additional CT32 record crosses only horizontally. Applying the tested source formulas conditionally yields an address discrepancy for the four CT32 vertical cases, without proving any observed texture corruption.
